topics.title: Start an asset review
topics.summary: Create a private project to describe what you have and organize supporting evidence. Opening a project does not verify the asset.
details: Begin with the exact item or right, your relationship to it, and the outcome you want. You can read the public guides before signing in.
Keep an owner-supplied statement separate from facts independently confirmed by a qualified source.

topics.title: Plain or professional explanations
topics.summary: Choose everyday language or more technical wording for introductory guides and public answers. The underlying evidence requirements stay the same.
details: You can switch styles as your understanding grows. This setting changes how explanations are presented; it does not approve an asset or change a review result.

topics.title: Your private workspace
topics.summary: Sign in with the approved account used for your workspace access. Public guides and general questions are available without signing in.
details: A project keeps documents, project conversations and released reports together according to your access. Having a sign-in link alone does not grant access.
Use the same approved email when choosing Google sign-in. Never enter a wallet private key or recovery phrase as an account credential.

topics.title: Choose the closest asset type
topics.summary: Choose the category that best describes the item or right. If you are unsure, preserve its exact wording and explain the uncertainty.
details: Bonds, bank instruments and physical property can start in the instrument category. Wallets, smart contracts and digital preparation have their own starting categories.
A category is an organizing choice, not a conclusion about authenticity, ownership or value.

topics.title: Understanding a bond
topics.summary: A bond describes a debt obligation under stated terms. Its printed face amount is not the same as current sale value or a confirmed payable balance.
details: Identify the issuer, exact issue, holder, maturity and current status. Obtain the appropriate issuer, registrar or custody evidence before relying on the claim.
An old or convincing certificate may require corporate-action, estate or redemption checks.

topics.title: What an SKR establishes
topics.summary: An SKR is a safekeeping receipt whose exact custody terms need checking. A receipt alone does not establish the contents, ownership, value or financing availability.
details: Ask what was received, whether it was inspected, what is held now, who may obtain delivery and which charges or claims apply.
Connect the receipt, custody agreement and identified property through direct confirmation from the appropriate custodian.

topics.title: Understanding an SBLC
topics.summary: An SBLC is a bank undertaking with specific terms and drawing conditions. Its stated amount is not unrestricted cash available to the beneficiary.
details: Identify the applicant, issuing bank, beneficiary, expiry, applicable terms and any advising or confirming bank. Verification should reach the bank through an independently established channel.
A message label or supplied SWIFT copy does not settle the undertaking, current availability or a lender’s decision.

topics.title: Inherited documents and authority
topics.summary: Inherited papers can be useful evidence, but the right to act for an estate or transfer an asset must also be established.
details: Preserve originals and identify the asset’s registration, the relevant estate or trust, and the person currently authorized to act.
A will, beneficiary arrangement, trust and court appointment can have different roles. The applicable process depends on the asset and jurisdiction.

topics.title: Gold: identity, custody and value
topics.summary: Identify whether the claim concerns physical metal, an account entitlement or another right. Testing, ownership, custody and valuation answer different questions.
details: Match bar or item identifiers, weight, stated fineness, inspection records and custody evidence. Use a test method suitable for the item and the claim.
A photograph, hallmark or price calculation alone does not establish the metal’s composition or availability for delivery.

topics.title: Gems: identify the actual stone
topics.summary: A gem report must be checked with its issuer and matched to the actual stone. Identification or grading is separate from ownership and achievable sale value.
details: Record the material, natural or laboratory-created origin where applicable, treatments, dimensions and identifying features.
A matching report number supports the report record; it does not alone establish that the seller holds the described stone.

topics.title: Minerals and underground resources
topics.summary: A mineral deposit or mining interest is a different claim from metal already available for delivery. Review the rights and technical report that support the claim.
details: Record the report’s author, qualifications, effective date, reporting standard and assumptions, along with the relevant property or mineral rights.
Do not describe an underground resource estimate as a deliverable vault inventory.

topics.title: When you do not know the name
topics.summary: Use the exact wording, markings and description you can observe. An unfamiliar label should remain a question until the item is properly classified.
details: Photograph both sides and preserve related records. Keep what someone told you separate from what the document or object actually shows.
Choose the appropriate specialist after clarifying the claim; do not infer a financial product from a nickname.

topics.title: Choose the appropriate professional
topics.summary: Match the professional to the question: legal authority, bank terms, physical testing, custody or market value may need different specialists.
details: Check the organization, qualifications, official contact route, engagement scope and the report it will provide.
A securities desk, trade-finance team and bullion specialist perform different functions. Interest from a contact is not a financing commitment.

topics.title: What a wallet can show
topics.summary: A public address can reveal ledger information on a specific network. Seeing a balance does not establish who controls it, owns it or may transfer it.
details: Start with the exact network and public address. Separate observed balance, control evidence, legal title and economic value.
Never provide private keys or recovery phrases to establish an asset claim.

topics.title: Review the exact smart contract
topics.summary: A token name or ticker is not enough to identify a contract. Record its network and exact address, then examine the relevant controls and restrictions.
details: The review may need to identify who can mint, pause, freeze, change fees or upgrade the contract. A proxy can point to separate implementation code.
A contract or ledger observation does not by itself establish off-chain asset backing or legal rights.

topics.title: What a token represents
topics.summary: Tokenization records or represents a defined right. The holder’s enforceable rights, responsible parties and redemption terms need to be clear.
details: Review the underlying asset, authority, custody, restrictions and proposed holder rights before considering issuance.
Creating a digital record does not establish the underlying asset’s authenticity, value or acceptance by a lender.

topics.title: The five-stage asset journey
topics.summary: Verify, structure, connect, settle and monitor describe distinct stages. Each stage requires its own evidence, responsible parties and approvals.
details: The current workspace organizes evidence, screening, review and preparation. A stage label is not proof that a financial transaction has occurred.
Follow the current availability notes beside each stage. External issuance, settlement and attestation arrangements require their own connections and terms.

topics.title: Verify the specific claim
topics.summary: Collect records and identify which facts need independent confirmation. Existence, ownership, custody, value and transferability must be assessed separately.
details: Screening can point out observations and missing information. Record who confirmed each fact, when, by which method and within what scope.

topics.title: Define the rights first
topics.summary: Describe exactly what right a holder would receive, against whom it can be enforced and what restrictions apply.
details: Link the proposed structure to ownership and authority evidence, custody arrangements, transfer terms and any redemption obligations.
Digital preparation in this workspace does not issue a token.

topics.title: Prepare a factual introduction
topics.summary: Build a sourced briefing for an appropriate professional, buyer or lender. Their eligibility and acceptance still need confirmation.
details: Separate known facts, owner-supplied claims and unresolved questions. Review every statement and the information intended for sharing.
Saving a contact or briefing does not send a message or create a commitment.

topics.title: Agree how the transfer completes
topics.summary: A completed transaction needs the responsible parties to agree on payment, delivery, rights transfer and any escrow or custody requirements.
details: Identify what must happen, who performs each step and what happens if a step fails.
This workspace does not move funds or complete settlement.

topics.title: Keep evidence current
topics.summary: An earlier confirmation describes its recorded scope and time. Review changes, expiry and unresolved conditions before relying on it again.
details: Identify the source, observation date, exact assertion and refresh requirements. A changed custody position or legal restriction can affect the next action.
External monitoring feeds are not connected merely because an evidence record exists.

topics.title: What an oracle can establish
topics.summary: An oracle relays information or an attestation from a source. Its output depends on that source’s scope and freshness.
details: Ask who made the assertion, what was checked, when it was checked and how it relates to the particular asset.
An oracle is not independent bond authentication, a valuation guarantee or a funding commitment. External attestation feeds are currently awaiting connection.

topics.title: Ask a general asset question
topics.summary: Ask about the published guides or how the site works. Use your private project for questions involving your documents or personal financial information.
details: The public assistant explains supported subjects and links to relevant reading. It does not inspect your holdings or certify an asset.
Choose Plain language or Professional terms above, then speak or type. If a question is unclear, try naming the asset and the specific point you want explained.

topics.title: Speak to Asset Machine
topics.summary: Tap the disc and allow microphone access, then tap it again to finish your question. You can always type instead.
details: A recording ends automatically after about 25 seconds. When the disc is preparing or speaking a reply, tapping it stops the current voice activity.
Keep the public question general. Do not speak account credentials, recovery phrases or private document details here.

topics.title: Stop the current voice activity
topics.summary: Stop ends the current public recording, pending reply or playback. If you were recording, use the disc to finish and submit your question instead.
details: The disc finishes a recording and asks the question; the separate Stop control cancels the current activity. You can start a new question afterward.

topics.title: Listen to the reply again
topics.summary: Play reply restarts the latest prepared spoken answer. The written answer and its reference links remain available for reading.
details: If your browser blocks automatic playback, press Play reply. If audio is unavailable, use the text and follow its linked sources.

topics.title: Sources, dates and scope
topics.summary: A source supports the particular statement within its scope. Check its date, jurisdiction and limitations before applying it to an asset claim.
details: Article links explain the subject; primary-source links take you to the underlying institution or publication. A research date is not a fresh confirmation of an individual holding.
Reading a source or finding a report number does not itself establish ownership, value or permission to transfer.

topics.title: The full knowledge base
topics.summary: Explore the detailed public reference library by topic or search term. Open Knowledge & help anywhere to read without leaving your current work.
details: The library covers evidence, bonds, SKRs, SBLCs, inherited assets, gold, gems, wallets and tokenization.
Use the article’s source links and scope notes for deeper checking. The library provides education, not a finding about a specific asset.

topics.title: Find a specific explanation
topics.summary: Search article titles, reference text and topic terms. A few precise words usually work best, such as SKR, assay, MT799 or redemption.
details: A selected topic narrows the results. Clear the query or choose All topics to broaden the search.
The public library searches published explanations, not your private project documents.

topics.title: Browse by subject
topics.summary: Choose a topic to narrow the library, then use search to find a specific question within it.
details: An article can belong to several topics when the same evidence issue affects more than one asset type. Choose All topics to restore the complete library.

topics.title: Use the evidence checklist
topics.summary: Download a working checklist to organize the records and confirmations needed for an asset review. A checked box needs supporting evidence.
details: Record the source, date, scope and unresolved questions for each relevant item. The checklist does not replace the appropriate professional’s examination or decision.

topics.title: Save a complete reference article
topics.summary: Download Markdown for formatted reuse or plain text for easy reading. Both include the article’s reference information and source links.
details: These downloads contain public educational material. They do not export your private project, uploaded documents or attorney work.

topics.title: Share the public explanation
topics.summary: Share or download the introductory guide for someone who needs context. The educational link or card does not include your private project details.
details: The explanation card is a short introduction; use the guide text or full knowledge article for more detail.
Sharing a guide is not an asset verification statement or permission to share client documents.

topics.title: Name your project clearly
topics.summary: Use a recognizable name for the holding or question. A project name is a label, not an authentication or valuation statement.
details: For example, identify the asset type and the review purpose without putting sensitive account credentials in the title.

topics.title: Describe the claim in your words
topics.summary: Explain what you believe you hold, how you obtained it and what you want to do. This is recorded as your statement until supporting evidence establishes the facts.
details: Include the exact document wording or observable features when the classification is uncertain. Distinguish what you saw from what someone else told you.

topics.title: Stated issuer or creator
topics.summary: Enter the issuer or creator as shown on the record. A printed name or logo still needs to be linked to the appropriate independent source.
details: Keep the issuer, intermediary and custodian distinct. If you are unsure which role a named organization has, say so in the description.

topics.title: Claimed amount versus current value
topics.summary: Record the amount and currency stated in the claim. Face value, an appraisal, a displayed balance and likely sale proceeds are different measures.
details: Use the description to identify where the figure came from and its date. Do not present an entered number as a verified valuation or financing offer.

topics.title: Record the stated date
topics.summary: Copy the issue date exactly as shown and explain any uncertainty. An old or recent date alone does not establish current validity.
details: Where several dates appear, distinguish issuance, maturity, inspection and confirmation dates in your description or evidence.

topics.title: Choose the correct blockchain network
topics.summary: The same-looking address or token name can appear on different networks. Choose the actual network relevant to the holding or contract.
details: The network and exact asset identifier must be assessed together. A supported selection does not by itself prove control, ownership or token value.

topics.title: Public wallet or contract address
topics.summary: Enter the public address for the selected network. Never enter a private key, recovery phrase or account password.
details: A public address lets a reviewer identify ledger information. It does not establish that you control the address or have legal authority to sell or pledge its assets.
For a token or NFT, the contract address and any applicable token ID may also be needed.

topics.title: Explain the intended next step
topics.summary: State the question you want resolved: identification, ownership, inheritance transfer, sale, redemption, financing or tokenization.
details: The intended action determines which evidence and specialist review are relevant. Asking for an outcome does not mean it is available or approved.

topics.title: Add particulars you can support
topics.summary: Add issuer, amount, dates and network details when you know them. You can leave unknown particulars blank and explain the gaps.
details: Keep uncertain information qualified. Supporting documents and independent confirmations are more useful than guessing a technical field.

topics.title: What the project status means
topics.summary: The status describes the project’s place in the review workflow. It is not an asset authenticity, value or financing rating.
details: A queued project awaits review steps. A released report means the approved report is available; its actual conclusions and limitations still control.

topics.title: Your next suggested action
topics.summary: The workspace suggests a next step from the documents, findings and reports currently recorded. Review the underlying evidence before acting.
details: Typical next steps are adding originals, checking extracted text, reviewing screening questions and reading an independently released report.

topics.title: Download the project action summary
topics.summary: This download summarizes the project description, document references, recorded findings and suggested next steps. It is separate from the released legal report.
details: The summary is generated from current project information and can include private project details. Review it before sharing.
It does not include private attorney notes or unreleased drafts. Download any released legal report separately from Legal review.

topics.title: Build the evidence file
topics.summary: Keep original records and a clear explanation of what each item supports. A document’s presence does not mean its contents have been independently verified.
details: For documents, include both sides and relevant attachments. For physical assets, connect photographs and reports to the specific item or inventory.
Record independent confirmations, their dates and any remaining gaps alongside the submitted material.

topics.title: Upload supporting originals
topics.summary: Add PDF, PNG, JPEG or text files, up to 10 MB each and 30 documents per project. Check that every file belongs to this project.
details: Include front and back where relevant. Keep the physical original safe and retain information about its source.
After upload, inspect the extracted text for errors in names, identifiers, dates and amounts.

topics.title: Inspect and correct extracted text
topics.summary: OCR is a working transcription and can misread important details. Correcting it changes the transcription; the original file remains intact.
details: Compare names, serial numbers, dates, decimal places and currency symbols with the original. Explain unclear or missing wording instead of inventing it.

topics.title: Download the uploaded original
topics.summary: Original downloads the source file stored with this project. Preserve it separately from any corrected transcription or later summary.
details: The original may contain private information. Check the intended recipient and sharing authority before sending it elsewhere.

topics.title: What the file hash proves
topics.summary: A SHA-256 hash helps check whether a file’s bytes match a recorded version. It does not establish that the document’s claims are true.
details: Use the hash alongside the file’s source, identity and review history. Matching bytes are not proof of asset ownership, authenticity or value.

topics.title: What automated screening does
topics.summary: Run screening to record observations, concerns and missing evidence from the available material. It does not authenticate an instrument or establish legal title.
details: Inspect extracted text first. Read each finding’s scope and source, then seek the appropriate independent confirmation for material claims.
A supported ledger observation is a technical finding at a point in time, not a complete asset or ownership review.

topics.title: Read each finding within its scope
topics.summary: A finding records an observation, concern or gap with a stated scope. A concern prompts further review; it is not automatically a fraud accusation.
details: Check what was examined, the source, the recorded date and the unanswered questions. Keep source-matched facts separate from claims still awaiting confirmation.

topics.title: Submit a project for legal review
topics.summary: Submission places the project in the review queue. Active legal review still requires accepted engagement and the applicable payment arrangements.
details: Organize the evidence and your questions before submitting. The attorney’s released report, not submission alone, provides the scoped legal analysis.

topics.title: Independent legal review
topics.summary: Legal review addresses the agreed questions and evidence within an accepted engagement. The displayed project review is subject to scope, conflicts and jurisdiction checks.
details: The standard review price shown here is $500 per project; additional representation is separate. Payment records and any applicable exemption are handled in the workspace.
Legal review does not automatically supply physical testing, issuer confirmation, valuation or financing acceptance.

topics.title: Accept the review engagement
topics.summary: The assigned reviewer confirms the agreed scope, applicable conflict check and ability to undertake the matter in the relevant jurisdiction.
details: Confirm each acknowledgment based on the actual professional checks. Accepting an engagement does not by itself approve the report or resolve missing evidence.

topics.title: Record a confirmed review payment
topics.summary: This records an independently confirmed external review-payment receipt. It does not charge a card or transfer money.
details: Enter the actual receipt or transaction reference only after confirming the payment through the agreed process. The acknowledgment records that confirmation.

topics.title: Private reviewer working notes
topics.summary: Use this area for the assigned reviewer’s working analysis. These notes are separate from the client report and are not released with it.
details: Keep the client-facing conclusions in the report draft. Save the review version when notes or the draft change.

topics.title: Prepare the client report draft
topics.summary: Write the analysis intended for the client, including the scope, evidence considered, conclusions and unresolved questions.
details: This is a working draft until the reviewer saves, approves and releases the appropriate version. Editing is not the same as releasing a report.

topics.title: Review every AI-assisted draft
topics.summary: Prepare AI draft creates suggested report text from the permitted case material. The assigned reviewer must check, edit and save it before approval.
details: Confirm factual statements, source references and missing-evidence qualifications. An AI draft does not approve itself or release a client report.
Save or copy current unsaved edits before replacing the draft.

topics.title: Save a review version
topics.summary: Save the current notes and draft as a review version. Saving preserves the work but does not approve or release it.
details: Approval applies to an exact saved version. After editing, save and review the resulting version before approval.

topics.title: Approve the exact saved report
topics.summary: Approval records the assigned reviewer’s judgment on the exact saved version. Unsaved changes must be resolved first.
details: Approval and release are separate steps. Changes to the relevant draft or evidence require renewed review rather than reliance on an earlier approval.

topics.title: Release the approved report
topics.summary: Release makes the approved report version available in the authenticated client portal. It does not send an external email.
details: Confirm the exact saved and approved version before releasing it. Clients see the released report, not private notes or unreleased drafts.

topics.title: Download the released legal report
topics.summary: Download the specific released report version shown here. Read its scope, findings and limitations before relying on it.
details: Earlier released versions may also appear. Check the version and release date, and treat the downloaded report as private project material.

topics.title: Listen to a text excerpt
topics.summary: Listen plays a limited excerpt of the displayed answer or report. Read or download the complete text for the full analysis and references.
details: Audio is a reading aid. It does not add a verification or professional approval to the underlying text.

topics.title: Prepare the next conversation
topics.summary: Record a prospective contact and a factual briefing from attributable sources. A saved prospect is not an introduction, endorsement or commitment.
details: Verify the person, organization, relevant services and authority independently. Keep claims about your asset within the evidence actually available.
Saving this information does not initiate outreach.

topics.title: Identify the actual contact
topics.summary: Record the person’s name, organization and professional email from a source you can verify. Do not assume a familiar name or domain establishes authority.
details: Keep the supporting source and unresolved identity questions in the briefing. Check contact details independently before sharing private material.

topics.title: Record the contact’s actual authority
topics.summary: Describe the person’s documented role and what decisions they can make. Interest in a proposal is not authority to approve funding or a transaction.
details: Separate a broker, introducer, adviser and final decision-maker. Note any authority that has not yet been independently established.

topics.title: Keep an attributable source
topics.summary: Enter a public HTTPS page that supports the contact’s identity, role or services. A pasted link is a reference to check, not independent confirmation.
details: Prefer an independently located official organization page or appropriate professional register. Record any facts the page does not establish.

topics.title: Explain the documented fit
topics.summary: Describe why the proposed conversation fits the contact’s publicly stated interests or services. Keep an assumption clearly labeled as an assumption.
details: Refer to specific evidence of the organization’s scope or eligibility requirements. Do not present likely interest as an agreed mandate or offer.

topics.title: Record the unresolved questions
topics.summary: List the counterparty checks completed and the issues still open, including identity, authority, service eligibility and proposed terms.
details: A concise record of what remains unknown is more useful than an unsupported claim that a contact or asset is fully verified.

topics.title: Download a draft briefing
topics.summary: The briefing organizes the proposed conversation and suggested opening. It remains a draft and has not been sent.
details: Review its claims, contact details and sharing permissions before using it. Private legal notes and reports are not automatically included.

topics.title: Understand the activity history
topics.summary: Project history records workflow actions and their times. It helps you follow what happened in the workspace.
details: An activity record is not independent confirmation of the underlying asset. Read the associated evidence and any released review for the substantive findings.

topics.title: Manage workspace access
topics.summary: Use the access controls available to your role to add permitted users or manage access. Saving access does not send an invitation email automatically.
details: The person must sign in with the approved account. Choose only the access appropriate to their actual responsibilities.

topics.title: Use the approved account email
topics.summary: Enter the email the person will use for their confirmed sign-in. A different Google account will not match the approved access.
details: Check the address carefully before saving. Share the sign-in link through your agreed process; saving an access record does not send an email.

topics.title: Choose the appropriate role
topics.summary: Clients work with their own projects and released reports; reviewers work on assigned legal matters; administrators manage projects within their permissions.
details: Only grant the role needed for the person’s responsibilities. Role assignment does not make private notes or unreleased drafts public.

topics.title: Permission to invite clients
topics.summary: This permission allows an administrator to invite clients when authorized. It does not grant authority to change privileged roles or waive payments.
details: An invitation still requires the recipient to authenticate with the approved email. Share the provided sign-in link after saving; no email is sent automatically.

topics.title: Site payment exemption
topics.summary: An authorized exemption changes the person’s applicable site-payment requirement. It does not establish that an external bill has been paid.
details: Only the owner can grant or change this setting. Engagement acceptance and professional review requirements remain separate.

topics.title: Suspend workspace access
topics.summary: Suspension stops the person’s workspace access. It does not delete their identity or the project’s evidence and review history.
details: Check the selected person and role before confirming. Access changes should match the owner’s authorized decision.

topics.title: Share the sign-in link
topics.summary: Copy the link for the intended person to open with the approved account. The link alone does not grant access.
details: No email is sent automatically. Verify the recipient and the approved account before sharing the link.

topics.title: Read each connection’s status
topics.summary: Available, connected, pending and not enabled describe different states. A pending service is not performed by opening or reviewing a project.
details: Check the relevant workflow’s current availability before promising an outcome. Evidence preparation does not by itself enable issuance, outreach, checkout or settlement.

topics.title: Ask about this project
topics.summary: The project assistant uses the case material permitted for your access and can point to public educational references. Its replies are drafts to review.
details: Ask about missing evidence, the meaning of a finding or a practical next step. Distinguish general education from facts established in this particular case.
An answer does not approve an asset, replace the assigned reviewer’s judgment or release a legal report.

topics.title: Dictate, then check the text
topics.summary: Record a short statement to add a transcription to the selected field. Check the words, names and numbers before saving or sending.
details: Use the recording control again to stop; short recordings end automatically. Microphone permission is required, and you can type instead.
Dictation adds working text. It does not save a review version or approve a report.

topics.title: Digital preparation record
topics.summary: This download contains preparation metadata linked to the project. It is not a minted token or a transferable financial instrument.
details: Define the underlying rights, authority, custody, restrictions and proposed responsibilities before any separate issuance decision.
The preparation record may contain private project information. Review it before sharing.

topics.title: The different meanings of proof
topics.summary: Evidence of existence, ownership, control, value, transferability and financeability answers different questions. One positive result does not establish all six.
details: Ask exactly what a record, test or confirmation proves and what remains unresolved. A screenshot, hash, certificate or token is not a complete asset verification by itself.
